title: House Votes on Russia Sanctions Bill Named for Lindsey Graham
summary: Imagine being so determined to stop a war that you spend a whole year working on a plan. That's what the late Sen. Lindsey Graham of South Carolina did. On Wednesday, the House voted on a big bill named after him. It would slap sanctions (penalties) on Russia to cut off money for its war in Ukraine. The bill goes after Russian officials, banks, and a 'shadow fleet' of tankers that sneak Russian oil around the world. It also tells President Donald Trump to charge up to 100% tariffs (taxes on imports) on the top five countries that buy Russian oil or gas. That's a huge tax — imagine paying double for something! Supporters say it will make countries like China and India think twice before buying Russian oil. Critics say it could hurt our friends in Europe and make prices go up here. Rep. Steny Hoyer said, 'If we fail to pass this bill, there will be cheers in the Kremlin and tears in Kyiv.' Ukraine's president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, has been pushing hard for it. If the House passes it, it goes to Trump to sign. This is the biggest move to help Ukraine since Trump came back to the White House.
why_it_matters: Punishing a country with money rules instead of soldiers is one of the main tools leaders use to try to stop wars — and those choices can change prices families pay at the store.

background_read: Ukraine (a country in Eastern Europe) has been fighting a war since Russia (the world's largest country) attacked it, and the United States and Europe have been sending it money and weapons.
The U.S. House of Representatives (one of the two parts of Congress, where lawmakers write and vote on laws) was voting on this bill; the Senate is the other part.
Lindsey Graham was a longtime U.S. senator from South Carolina who worked for a whole year on a plan to punish Russia, which is why the bill carries his name.
Article_Structure: WHO: The U.S. House of Representatives, voting on a bill named for the late Sen. Lindsey Graham of South Carolina.

WHAT: A bill that puts sanctions on Russian officials, banks, and a 'shadow fleet' of oil tankers, and tells President Donald Trump to charge up to 100% tariffs on the top five buyers of Russian oil or gas.
WHERE: The vote happens in the U.S. House, but the effects are aimed at Russia, Ukraine, and buyer countries like China and India.
WHY: Supporters want to cut off money for Russia's war in Ukraine; critics worry it could hurt friends in Europe and raise prices in the U.S.

perspectives.description: They say the bill makes countries like China and India think twice before buying Russian oil, so Russia has less money for its war.
They worry the new tariffs could hurt friendly countries in Europe and make things more expensive here at home.
Ukraine's president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, has pushed hard for the bill, hoping it brings more help against Russia.
